facts.fact: Kharif is the June–September monsoon season.
Raniganj, Jharia and Bokaro lie in the Damodar valley.
Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port.
Shifting cultivation is Podu in AP and Jhumming in the north-east.
Karnataka leads coffee, Kerala rubber, Assam tea.
Groundnut is a kharif crop giving about half of oilseeds; jowar is the third food crop.
White–milk, Yellow–oilseeds, Blue–fisheries, Golden Fibre–jute.
Magnetite has a higher iron content than hematite; Odisha leads iron ore.
Bauxite–Koraput, copper–Malanjkhand, mica–Gudur, barytes–Mangampeta.
Mumbai High (ONGC), Digboi first refinery, KG basin.
Simhadri thermal, Srisailam and Nagarjunasagar hydel, Kurnool solar park are AP power plants.
Bhabha's three-stage nuclear programme ends with thorium.
Bhadla solar park; Muppandal wind farm in Tamil Nadu.
Geothermal energy is non-conventional.
Broad gauge is 1,676 mm.
National Highways are about 2% of roads but carry about 40% of traffic.
NW-1 is the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly.
The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor is AP's key corridor.
City of Destiny – Visakhapatnam; Manchester of India – Ahmedabad.
Rabi crops are sown in winter (wheat, gram, mustard).
Monazite (Kerala sands), uranium (Jaduguda), gold (Kolar), diamond (Panna).
Ports are major (central) or non-major (state); Sagarmala is port-led development.
Land of the Rising Sun Japan; Midnight Sun Norway; Thunder Dragon Bhutan; Emerald Isle Ireland.
Temperate grasslands are the world's wheat and livestock belts.
Ruhr, North American Manufacturing Belt, Kanto, Lancashire.
Australia leads iron ore (Pilbara); Chile copper (Escondida).
Corn Belt, dairy, Mediterranean and extensive grain farming.
South Coast Railway is the 18th zone (HQ Visakhapatnam), with Guntakal, Guntur and Vijayawada divisions.
AP is developing greenfield ports at Ramayapatnam, Mulapeta, Machilipatnam and Kakinada SEZ.
Bhogapuram airport is named after Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Fishing grounds form where warm and cold currents meet over broad shelves.
Weber's least-cost theory; iron and steel is raw-material-oriented.
Neem-coated urea slows urea dissolution in soil.
India's geographical area is about 328.7 million ha, of which about 305 million ha is reporting area.
Net sown area is about 140 million ha (about 46% of reporting area); gross cropped area about 200 million ha (recent land-use data; our source gives 143 and 180 million ha).
Cropping intensity = gross cropped area ÷ net sown area × 100; India's is about 155%.
Only about half of India's net sown area is irrigated; the rest is rain-fed.
Dryland farming is practised where annual rainfall is below 75 cm; wetland (rain-fed) farming where rain exceeds crop needs.
Protective irrigation supplements rain to save crops; productive irrigation maximises yield with ample water.
Wheat and barley farming with cattle, sheep and goats appears at Mehrgarh by 8000–6000 BCE; the animal-drawn plough dates to about 2500 BCE (Indus).
About 86% of Indian farmers are small and marginal (under 2 ha).
Cropping systems: mono-, inter-, mixed, sequential, relay (second crop sown before the first is harvested) and multiple cropping.
Zaid crops (March–June) include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber and vegetables.
In Assam, West Bengal and Odisha three rice crops — Aus (autumn), Aman (winter) and Boro (summer) — are grown a year.
The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture promotes climate-resilient farming and PKVY promotes organic farming.
Shifting cultivation is called jhum(ming) in the north-east (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland).
It is called pamlou in Manipur.
It is called dipa in Bastar (Chhattisgarh).
It is called bewar/dahiya in Madhya Pradesh.
It is called podu/penda in Andhra Pradesh.
It is called pama dabi, koman or bringa in Odisha.
It is called khil in the Himalayan belt and kuruwa in Jharkhand.
Abroad it is milpa (Mexico/Central America), conuco (Venezuela), ladang (Indonesia) and ray (Vietnam).
Rice: 22–32°C, 150–300 cm rain, clayey-loamy soil; leading states West Bengal > Uttar Pradesh > Punjab; India 2nd after China; largest exporter.
Wheat: 10–15°C sowing, 21–26°C ripening, 75–100 cm; leading states Uttar Pradesh > Madhya Pradesh > Punjab; India 2nd after China; rabi.
Jowar: rain-fed, 50–100 cm; leading states Maharashtra > Karnataka; third food crop by area.
Bajra: sandy and shallow black soils; leading states Rajasthan > Uttar Pradesh > Gujarat; most drought-hardy millet.
Ragi: red, black, sandy soils of dry regions; rich in iron and calcium; leading states Karnataka > Tamil Nadu; nutri-cereal.
Maize: 21–27°C, old alluvium; leading states Karnataka > Madhya Pradesh > Maharashtra; food and fodder; also for starch and ethanol.
Pulses: 20–27°C, 25–60 cm, sandy loam; legumes fix nitrogen (except arhar); leading states Madhya Pradesh > Rajasthan > Maharashtra; India largest producer, consumer and importer.
Sugarcane: 21–27°C, hot-humid, 75–100 cm; leading states Uttar Pradesh > Maharashtra > Karnataka; India 2nd after Brazil.
Soybean: kharif oilseed of the Malwa plateau; leading states Madhya Pradesh > Maharashtra; MP called the "Soya State".
Rapeseed-mustard: rabi oilseed; leading states Rajasthan > Haryana > Madhya Pradesh; Rajasthan leads.
Groundnut: kharif oilseed, about half of oilseed output; leading states Gujarat > Rajasthan > Tamil Nadu; Saurashtra the heartland.
Tea: 20–30°C, 150–300 cm, well-drained humus-rich slopes; leading states Assam > West Bengal > Tamil Nadu; India 2nd producer, largest consumer; Tea Board Kolkata.
Coffee: 15–28°C, 150–250 cm, shaded slopes; leading states Karnataka > Kerala > Tamil Nadu; brought from Yemen to Baba Budan hills; Coffee Board Bengaluru.
Rubber: above 25°C, over 200 cm, equatorial crop; leading states Kerala > Tripura; Rubber Board Kottayam.
Cotton: 21–30°C, 50–100 cm, 210 frost-free days, black soil; leading states Gujarat > Maharashtra > Telangana; India among the top producers; Bt cotton.
Jute: 25–35°C, 150–250 cm, delta alluvium; leading states West Bengal > Bihar > Assam; India largest producer; "golden fibre".

Spices: cardamom (Idukki), pepper (Kerala–Karnataka), saffron (Pampore, J&K); leading states Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana; India largest producer, consumer and exporter; Spices Board Kochi.
Fruits and vegetables: about 13% of world vegetables; leading states Uttar Pradesh (mango, potato), Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh; India 2nd producer after China.
Andhra Pradesh is India's largest chilli producer; Guntur (Sannam chilli, GI) has Asia's largest chilli market yard.
Prakasam–Guntur (Ongole region) grows Virginia flue-cured (FCV) tobacco; the Tobacco Board is at Guntur.
Andhra Pradesh is India's largest oil palm producer (Eluru–West Godavari).
Banganapalle mango (Nandyal–Kurnool, GI) is AP's premium mango.
Araku Valley Arabica coffee (GI, 2019) is grown by tribal farmers of the Eastern Ghats.
Anantapur is AP's groundnut district (Scarce Rainfall zone).
Konaseema (Godavari delta) is AP's coconut belt.
Andhra Pradesh leads India in aquaculture — shrimp and freshwater fish (West Godavari–Krishna–Nellore).
Duggirala (Guntur) is a turmeric market of AP.
The Krishna–Godavari delta is AP's rice bowl; AP is a top-five rice state.
The Green Revolution (1960s; M.S. Swaminathan, Norman Borlaug's HYV wheat) raised wheat and rice output in Punjab–Haryana–western UP.
Operation Flood (White Revolution, 1970) under Verghese Kurien (NDDB, Anand) made India the world's largest milk producer.
The Blue Revolution concerns fisheries; India is the second-largest fish producer.
The Yellow Revolution (Technology Mission on Oilseeds, 1986) concerns oilseeds (Sam Pitroda associated).
The Pink Revolution concerns meat/poultry processing (and onions); the Silver Revolution eggs/poultry.
The Golden Revolution concerns horticulture and honey; the Golden Fibre Revolution jute; the Silver Fibre Revolution cotton.
The Brown Revolution concerns leather/cocoa and non-conventional energy; the Grey Revolution fertilisers; the Red Revolution meat and tomato.
The Round Revolution concerns potato.
2023 was the International Year of Millets (India-proposed); millets are branded "Shree Anna".
MIDH and Project CHAMAN support horticulture; ISOPOM supported oilseeds, pulses, oil palm and maize.
Metallic minerals are ferrous (iron ore, manganese, chromite, nickel) or non-ferrous (copper, bauxite, lead, zinc, gold).
Tin, copper, zinc and lead occur in veins and lodes of igneous/metamorphic rocks.
Coal, iron ore, gypsum and potash occur in beds of sedimentary rock.
Bauxite is a residual deposit left by rock decomposition.
Gold, silver, tin and platinum occur as placer deposits in river sands.
India's mineral belts: the north-eastern plateau (Chotanagpur–Odisha), the south-western plateau (Karnataka–Goa), the north-western Aravalli belt and the Himalayan belt.
The Aravalli (Dharwar) belt of Rajasthan is rich in copper and zinc, marble, gypsum and Fuller's earth.
Iron-ore grades: magnetite (up to ~70% iron, finest), hematite (most used, ~50–70%), limonite (40–60%), siderite (<40%); our source rates hematite highest.
Chalcopyrite (about 34.5% copper) is the main copper ore; argentite the main silver ore.
Gibbsite is the high-alumina form of bauxite; boehmite and diaspore are harder to process.
Barbil–Koira valley (Kendujhar–Sundargarh, Odisha) is a leading iron-ore belt; Odisha is the top iron-ore state.
Bailadila (Dantewada, Chhattisgarh) is famed for high-grade iron ore exported via Visakhapatnam.
Dalli-Rajhara (Chhattisgarh) is a mechanised iron-ore mine feeding Bhilai.
Kudremukh (Karnataka) produced magnetite iron ore (now closed); Ballari–Hospet hematite is active.
Noamundi and Gua (Singhbhum, Jharkhand) are iron-ore mines.
Nagpur–Bhandara (Maharashtra) and Balaghat (MP) are manganese belts; Odisha leads output.
Sukinda valley (Jajpur, Odisha) holds almost all of India's chromite and nickeliferous limonite.
Koraput–Panchpatmali (Odisha) is India's biggest bauxite belt (NALCO); Odisha leads bauxite.
Lohardaga and Gumla (Jharkhand) and Junagadh (Gujarat) are bauxite areas.
Malanjkhand (Balaghat, MP) is India's largest copper mine; MP leads copper output.
Khetri (Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan) is a historic copper belt; Singhbhum (Jharkhand) also has copper.
Zawar (Udaipur, Rajasthan) yields lead, zinc and silver; Rampura-Agucha is the world's largest zinc mine.
Hutti (Raichur, Karnataka) is India's main working gold mine; Kolar is historic.
Jaduguda (Singhbhum, Jharkhand) was India's first uranium mine (UCIL); Tummalapalle (AP) is a large new reserve.
Koderma (Jharkhand) is the "Mica Capital"; Andhra Pradesh (Gudur–Nellore) is the top mica producer; Bhilwara (Rajasthan) also mines mica.
Panna (MP) has India's only working diamond mine (NMDC Majhgawan).
Rajasthan (Jodhpur, Bikaner, Nagaur, Jaisalmer) leads gypsum production.
Limestone for cement: Rajasthan, MP (Satna, Katni), AP (Kadapa), Chhattisgarh and Gujarat; Satna is a cement hub.
Lithium resources were reported at Salal-Haimana, Reasi (J&K) in 2023.
The National Critical Mineral Mission (2025) aims to secure lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other critical minerals.
Monazite beach sands (Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, AP) are India's thorium source; IREL processes them.
Mangampet (Kadapa region, AP) holds the world's largest single barytes deposit.
Coal ranks by carbon: peat (<40%), lignite (40–55%), bituminous (most used), anthracite (80–95%, J&K).
Gondwana coal (about 200–250 million years old) is ~98% of reserves; Tertiary coal (about 55 million years) occurs in the north-east.
The Damodar valley holds Raniganj (oldest, 1774), Jharia (largest coking coal), Bokaro, Giridih and Karanpura coalfields.
Other coalfields: Korba (Chhattisgarh), Talcher (Odisha), Singrauli (MP–UP), Chanda–Wardha (Maharashtra), Singareni (Telangana).
Lignite is mined at Neyveli (Tamil Nadu), and in Gujarat (Kutch), Rajasthan (Barsingsar, Palana) and J&K.
Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves; Odisha and Chhattisgarh lead coal production with Jharkhand.
Rat-hole mining is a hazardous narrow-pit coal mining method in Meghalaya (banned by the NGT in 2014).
Commercial coal mining by private firms was opened in 2020.
Coal supplies about 70% of India's electricity; Indian coal is high in ash.
Mumbai High, about 160 km offshore, was discovered in 1974 and is India's largest oil field (ONGC).
Gujarat's oil fields include Ankleshwar, Kalol, Mehsana, Nawagam and Kosamba.
Assam (Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran) is India's oldest oil region; Digboi has the oldest refinery (1901).
Barmer (Rajasthan, Mangala field) is India's largest onshore oil producer (Cairn–Vedanta).
The Krishna–Godavari basin (offshore KG-D6) and Cauvery basin are the main east-coast oil and gas basins.
Reliance's Jamnagar (Gujarat) is the world's largest refining complex.
The second refinery came up at Trombay (Mumbai) in 1954 (our source wrongly says Tarapur).
Strategic Petroleum Reserves are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur; Chandikhol (Odisha) is planned.
GAIL (1984) is India's largest natural-gas company, a Maharatna PSU.
LNG is natural gas cooled to about −160°C; CNG is compressed to 200–250 kg/cm².
Naharkatiya–Nunmati–Barauni was India's first crude pipeline.
The Hazira–Bijaipur–Jagdishpur (HBJ) pipeline was India's first cross-state gas pipeline.
Jamnagar–Loni is among the world's longest LPG pipelines.
Salaya–Mathura is a major crude pipeline from the Gujarat coast to Mathura refinery.
Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga (Jagdishpur–Haldia–Bokaro–Dhamra) brings gas to eastern India.
The Motihari–Amlekhganj pipeline (2019) to Nepal was South Asia's first cross-border petroleum pipeline.
The India–Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline (Siliguri–Parbatipur, 2023) carries diesel to Bangladesh.
The Kandla–Bathinda pipeline carries products from Gujarat to Punjab.
The National Gas Grid and City Gas Distribution networks extend PNG and CNG; PNGRB regulates pipelines.
Vindhyachal (Singrauli, MP; NTPC, 4,760 MW) is India's largest coal power station.
Mundra (Gujarat) hosts the second-largest thermal station and Tata's Mundra Ultra Mega Power Plant.
Talcher Super Thermal (Odisha) was the first mega power plant in our source.
Simhadri Super Thermal (NTPC, near Visakhapatnam) is a major AP station; Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS is at Vijayawada (Ibrahimpatnam) and Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS at Krishnapatnam.
Koyna (Maharashtra, ~1,960 MW) is India's largest completed hydroelectric project.
Shivanasamudra (Karnataka, 1902) on the Kaveri was India's (and Asia's) first major hydel station; Darjeeling had electricity in 1897.
Nathpa Jhakri (Sutlej, HP) is India's largest underground hydel project.
Subansiri Lower (Arunachal–Assam, 2,000 MW, NHPC) is India's largest hydel project under commissioning.
Tarapur (Maharashtra, 1969, US-built BWRs) was India's first nuclear power station.
Rawatbhata (RAPS, Rajasthan, 1973) was built with Canadian help (CANDU type).
Madras Atomic Power Station, Kalpakkam (1983–84) was India's first indigenous nuclear plant; the PFBR there is run by BHAVINI.
Narora (UP, 1991) is a nuclear plant on the Ganga.
Kakrapar (Gujarat) has India's first indigenous 700 MWe PHWR.
Kaiga (Karnataka, 2000) is a nuclear plant on the Kali river.
Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, 2013) has Russian VVER reactors and is India's largest nuclear plant.
Gorakhpur (Haryana), Mahi Banswara (Rajasthan), Jaitapur (Maharashtra) and Kovvada (Srikakulam, AP) are planned nuclear sites.
Bhadla Solar Park (Jodhpur, Rajasthan, ~2,245 MW) is among the world's largest solar parks.
Pavagada (Shakti Sthala, Karnataka, ~2,050 MW) is a giant solar park.
Rewa Ultra Mega Solar (MP, 750 MW) supplies the Delhi Metro and pioneered grid parity.
Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park (Panyam, AP, 1,000 MW, 2017) was among the largest single-location solar parks.
Kamuthi (Tamil Nadu, 648 MW, Adani) is a large single-site solar plant.
Khavda Renewable Energy Park (Rann of Kutch, Gujarat; 30 GW planned) will be the world's largest renewable park.
Muppandal (Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, ~1,500 MW) is India's largest onshore wind farm.
Jaisalmer Wind Park (Rajasthan, Suzlon, ~1,064 MW) is the second-largest wind farm.
Manikaran (Parvati valley, HP) and Puga–Chumathang (Ladakh) are geothermal sites; a 20 kW pilot plant runs at Manuguru (Telangana, SCCL).
The Gulf of Khambhat (tidal range ~11 m) and Gulf of Kutch (~8 m) have India's best tidal-power potential; the Sundarbans suit small plants.
Coal-fired plants generate about 75% of India's electricity (Korba, Singrauli, Kahalgaon are major sites).
Coal plants run at 35–38% efficiency; supercritical and ultra-supercritical plants reach up to about 48%.
Thermal plants locate near coal, water, rail links and load centres, needing 3–4 ha of land per MW.
India ranks about 5th in installed hydropower; large hydro (>25 MW) is under the Ministry of Power, small hydro (≤25 MW) under MNRE.
Small hydro sub-classes: micro (≤100 kW), mini (101 kW–2 MW), small (2–25 MW).
Apsara (BARC, August 1956) was Asia's first research reactor; CIRUS (1960) came with Canadian help.
The Atomic Energy Act was passed in 1962; AERB (1983) regulates nuclear safety; NPCIL owns and runs all power reactors except the PFBR.
India tested at Pokhran in 1974 (Smiling Buddha) and 1998 (Operation Shakti); the NSG waiver came in 2008.
Bhabha's three stages: PHWRs (natural uranium) → fast breeders (plutonium-239, sodium-cooled) → thorium reactors (uranium-233).
The Nuclear Energy Mission (Budget 2025) targets 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047, including small modular reactors.
Uranium mines of the Singhbhum belt: Jaduguda (first), Bhatin, Narwapahar, Turamdih.
India's COP26 "Panchamrit": 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030 and net zero by 2070.
Non-fossil sources crossed 50% of India's installed power capacity in 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 NDC goal.
India is about 4th in wind and 3rd in solar installed capacity worldwide.
The National Solar Mission (2010) is one of eight missions of the NAPCC.
PM-KUSUM (2019) gives farmers solar pumps and grid-connected solar plants.
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) funds rooftop solar for 1 crore homes (up to 300 free units a month).
The National Wind–Solar Hybrid Policy came in 2018; offshore wind policy (draft 2020) targets Gujarat and Tamil Nadu coasts.
Green Energy Corridors build transmission to evacuate renewable power.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission (January 2023) targets 5 MMT of green hydrogen a year by 2030.
The International Solar Alliance (2015, India–France) is headquartered at Gurugram.
GSI's Geothermal Atlas (2022) estimates about 10,600 MW of geothermal potential in about 340 hot springs across seven provinces.
Tidal power uses barrages, floodgate dams or tidal-stream generators.
Central Railway is headquartered at Mumbai CSMT (our source wrongly says Churchgate).
Western Railway is headquartered at Churchgate, Mumbai.
East Central Railway is headquartered at Hajipur.
East Coast Railway is headquartered at Bhubaneswar.
West Central Railway is headquartered at Jabalpur.
South Central Railway is headquartered at Secunderabad.
Northeast Frontier Railway is headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati.
North Eastern Railway is headquartered at Gorakhpur.
South Western Railway is headquartered at Hubballi (our source says Bengaluru).
North Central Railway is headquartered at Prayagraj.
South East Central Railway is headquartered at Bilaspur.
North Western Railway is headquartered at Jaipur.
South Eastern Railway (Garden Reach) and Eastern Railway and Metro Railway are headquartered in Kolkata.
South Coast Railway (18th zone) is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.
Gauges: broad 1,676 mm, metre 1,000 mm, narrow 762 mm, light 610 mm; standard gauge (1,435 mm) is used in the UK and for metros.
The Mountain Railways of India — Darjeeling Himalayan (1999), Nilgiri (2005) and Kalka–Shimla (2008) — are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Eastern DFC runs Ludhiana–Dankuni (coal, industry); the Western DFC Dadri–JNPT (containers).
The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (about 508 km) is India's first bullet-train project (Japanese Shinkansen).
Vande Bharat (Train 18), India's first indigenous semi-high-speed train, began on New Delhi–Varanasi in 2019.
The Chenab Bridge (USBRL, Reasi, J&K; about 359 m above the river), the world's highest railway arch bridge, opened in June 2025.
The new Pamban bridge (April 2025) is India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge.
Hubballi (Sri Siddharoodha Swamiji) station has the world's longest railway platform (about 1,507 m); our source names Gorakhpur.
Indian Railways (about 68,000 route km, 7,000+ stations) is the world's fourth-largest network.
Mission Raftaar aimed to raise average speeds to 50 km/h (freight) and 80 km/h (passenger).
Palace on Wheels and Maharajas' Express are luxury tourist trains.
India's road network (about 63 lakh km) is the world's second-largest; National Highways (about 1.46 lakh km, ~2% of length) carry ~40% of traffic.
NH-44 (Srinagar–Kanyakumari, about 4,112 km) is the longest National Highway.
The Golden Quadrilateral (about 5,846 km) joins Delhi–Mumbai–Chennai–Kolkata; the North–South (Srinagar–Kanyakumari) and East–West (Porbandar–Silchar) corridors total about 7,300 km.
Bharatmala Pariyojana (Phase I about 34,800 km) subsumed the NHDP; Setu Bharatam removes level crossings; the Green Highways Policy dates from 2015.
The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km, under Rohtang, 2020) is the world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft.
The Sela Tunnel (Arunachal, March 2024) is the world's longest twin-lane tunnel above 13,000 ft.
Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, about 21.8 km, January 2024) is India's longest sea bridge.
The Bhupen Hazarika (Dhola–Sadiya) bridge over the Lohit (about 9.15 km) is among India's longest river bridges; Bogibeel (Dibrugarh) is the longest rail-cum-road bridge.
The Char Dham project links Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri.
FASTag provides electronic toll collection; PMGSY builds rural roads and the BRO border roads.
India has 12 operational major ports; Vadhavan (Maharashtra), approved in 2024, will be the 13th (our source lists 13 with Haldia counted separately).
JNPA (Nhava Sheva) is the largest container port among major ports.
Mundra (Gujarat, Adani) is India's largest commercial (private) port.
Deendayal (Kandla), a tidal port in the Gulf of Kutch, handles the most cargo among major ports.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee (Kolkata) port is the oldest operating riverine port; Haldia is its dock complex.
Kamarajar (Ennore) was India's first corporatised major port.
Mormugao (Goa) is a leading iron-ore export port.
Paradip (Odisha) is a deep-water port exporting iron ore and importing coal and crude.
Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked, protected major port of the east coast.
Vizhinjam (Kerala, commissioned 2025) is India's first deep-water container transhipment port.
V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) is a major port of southern Tamil Nadu.
The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 National Waterways; IWAI (1986, Noida) develops them.
NW-2 is the Brahmaputra from Dhubri to Sadiya (891 km).
NW-3 is the West Coast Canal, Kottapuram–Kollam (205 km), Kerala.
NW-4 (1,078 km) joins Kakinada to Puducherry through the Godavari, Krishna and Buckingham Canal.
NW-5 (588 km) links Talcher–Dhamra–Paradip through the Brahmani and Mahanadi delta.
The Jal Marg Vikas Project (World Bank) develops NW-1 from Varanasi to Haldia; Sagarmala drives port-led development with Coastal Economic Zones.
India's first commercial flight was the 1911 Allahabad–Naini airmail; J.R.D. Tata flew Karachi–Bombay in 1932 (Tata Airlines, later Air India).
Air India returned to the Tata group in January 2022.
UDAN (2016) subsidises regional flights; NCAP 2016 allows 100% FDI; GAGAN (ISRO–AAI) is India's satellite-based augmentation system.
New greenfield airports include Mopa (Goa), Navi Mumbai and Noida (Jewar); Bhogapuram serves north-coastal AP.
The Airports Authority of India was formed in 1995; Delhi IGI is the busiest airport.
Geostationary satellites orbit about 35,786 km above the equator; MEO (2,000–35,786 km) serve navigation; LEO (500–2,000 km) serve broadband and observation.
BharatNet (from NOFN) aims to connect all ~2.5 lakh gram panchayats with optical fibre.
PM-WANI lets local Public Data Office Aggregators offer public Wi-Fi.
C-DOT developed GPON for BharatNet and the WiDHWAN mesh network.
Undersea fibre cables carry about 99% of international data.
India launched 5G services in October 2022.
PMGDISHA aims at rural digital literacy under Digital India.
